claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; components inside it inherit the package's version.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from Pulumi.yaml can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit).
An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically with per-language SDKs published to npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents.
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; this is Pulumi's recommended approach.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo containing one giant package for all components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
Links to referenced docs pages (packages concepts, components, packaging-components anchors, private-registry, pulumi_package_publish, publishing-packages) exist.
